Chapter 5. Compassion for Self and Others: The Heart of Transformation.
Let’s take a moment to talk about something that sits right at the center of real change: compassion—for yourself, and for the people around you.
Think about it. As you start noticing your own patterns and making moves toward growth, there’s a new challenge waiting for you. How do you actually respond to yourself—and to others—with kindness, instead of criticism?
Most of us are our own toughest critics. We see our mistakes, our fears, the things we wish we’d done differently. And what do we do? We judge, we push ourselves harder. But what if there’s another way?
The Enneagram gives us that way. It invites us to start with self-compassion, and let it ripple outward.
Now, it’s so easy to slip into using the Enneagram as a weapon. Maybe you’ve seen this—someone figures out their type, and suddenly they’re using it to excuse their worst habits, or to label and criticize everyone else. But honestly, that’s not what this tool is for.
The real magic of the Enneagram is empathy. When you see your own struggles, your own patterns, it’s a lot easier to remember that everyone else is carrying something too.
I’m reminded of a story. There was someone who always felt they had to be strong. Never showing weakness, never asking for help. On the outside, they seemed unbreakable—but inside, they were running on empty. When they discovered their type’s fear of vulnerability, it was like a light switched on. Their strength, they realized, had become a mask. Bit by bit, they learned to let that guard down. It wasn’t easy, but it brought a sense of relief—and a deeper connection with others.
Self-compassion isn’t about ignoring your flaws or pretending everything’s fine. It’s about seeing yourself honestly—patterns, fears, all of it—and choosing kindness anyway.
Most of us are quick to offer comfort when a friend is hurting. But when it’s our own pain? We’re not nearly as gentle. The Enneagram asks us to treat ourselves with the same understanding we’d offer someone we care about.
And here’s the beautiful part—when you start practicing compassion with yourself, it naturally spills over to others. Suddenly, it’s easier to see that, just like you, other people are acting from their own fears and motivations.
Maybe that colleague who seems distant is just trying to protect themselves from disappointment. Or the friend who never says no? Maybe they’re terrified of being left out.
The Enneagram helps us look past the surface and respond with empathy, instead of jumping to judgment.
I can’t help but think of a family gathering—not so long ago—where everyone slipped right back into their old roles. One person trying to keep the peace, another pushing for control, someone else pulling away in silence. In the past, that would’ve ended in hurt feelings and frustration. But with the Enneagram in mind, there was a new understanding. Each person was just doing their best, shaped by their own fears and hopes. That understanding brought patience—and a little more grace.
Transformation isn’t about becoming perfect. It’s about waking up, being more compassionate, and finding more freedom in how you show up.
The Enneagram gives you a map, but your journey? It’s your own. Some days you’ll breeze through. Others will feel tough.
But with every step, it gets a little easier to see yourself—and everyone else—with kindness.
